tonight.headline: Down 22.6 before you've played. Nothing to change today
body: Christian Watson's 22.6 from Thursday is all Footballers have. ESPN projects you 134.4 to their 128.6, a 53% chance. Your lineup as set is the projection lineup.

Nothing changed overnight. Warren and Coker are still questionable and expected to play. The two cards below only matter if one of them is inactive on Sunday. Check inactives yourself about 09:30 Mexico City, because the Sunday brief runs before they're out.

case.label: Their tight end
case.body: Brock Bowers was limited Wednesday and Thursday and sat Friday. Klint Kubiak called it planned rest, and he's questionable (DraftSharks). If he sits, their best replacement is on the wire, not their bench.

case.label: Their quarterback
case.body: Matthew Stafford starts for them. Their bench quarterback is Caleb Williams, whom the Bears have ruled out with a hamstring (Chicago Sun-Times), so they have no quarterback cover.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Coker or Warren inactive on Sunday with you not making the swap. Each is about 11-15 points you'd give away. The cards cover both.

doFirst.title: Only if Coker is inactive: start McLaurin in the flex
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed. Don't do this today. Swap only, nothing dropped. Coker is questionable but expected to play.

case.label: The ankle
case.body: Coker missed Thursday's practice and was limited Friday. Carolina list him questionable, and DraftSharks and NBC Sports call him expected to play. Xavier Legette is also questionable (ESPN).

case.label: Why McLaurin, not Boston
case.body: McLaurin projects 11.8 and drew 9 targets in Week 2. Boston projects 11.3 and drew 7 (week archive). That's close on both, so I take the projection and write no thesis. McLaurin faces Seattle, who have allowed the fewest WR points (footballdb, standard, Weeks 1-2), with Marcus Mariota throwing.

case.label: The clock
case.body: Coker, McLaurin and Boston all kick off Sunday 11:00 Mexico City, and inactives come out about 09:30. The Sunday brief runs at 07:00, before them.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker is active on Sunday. The card then never fires and costs nothing.

case.label: The shoulder
case.body: Warren was limited all week and is questionable. RotoWire and DraftSharks both say he should play. Rico Dowdle is OUT, and Still Curtain say Travis Homer is next behind a banged-up Warren.

case.label: Why Tuten
case.body: He is the only other back on your roster who plays Sunday at 11:00. Monangai is Monday night and Kamara plays in a three-way committee at 14:25.

case.body: Warren is active on Sunday. The card then never fires.

whatWentWrong.title: Two starters are still questionable at 11:00 kickoffs
whatWentWrong.lead: Coker (ankle) and Warren (shoulder) both go into Sunday questionable. The 07:00 Sunday brief can't see inactives, so the check is yours to make.

case.label: The gap
case.body: Inactives come out about 90 minutes before kickoff, about 09:30 Mexico City. Every brief runs before or after that window, so it can't answer for you.

case.label: The fix
case.body: The two cards above. Each is a swap, nothing dropped, and each fires only on an inactive.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Both active. Then neither card fires and there's nothing to do.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: FantasyPros' Week 3 board has McPherson K1, Trey Smack K2 and your Pineiro K3. ESPN projects Pineiro 9.4 to McPherson's 7.4.

case.label: Why hold
case.body: Pineiro came in on 23 Sep. Moving him would be the second change to that seat in a week, for no gain.

case.label: When to act
case.body: After 30 September, when the churn window closes, and only if Pineiro finishes Week 3 outside the top twenty kickers while McPherson finishes top five.

worthALook.name: Lions D/ST
worthALook.lead: The D/ST comparison. Hold the Vikings.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: ESPN has the Lions 7.8 to the Vikings' 7.7. The Lions are on waivers until Sunday 01:00 Mexico City. The Vikings face Tampa Bay, 30th in points given to defences. The Lions face the Jets, 7th-fewest (footballdb).

case.label: Why hold
case.body: A 0.1 gap isn't a reason to touch a seat that has changed hands three times since 23 Sep.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing this week. If the Vikings finish outside the top fifteen while the Lions finish top five, revisit when the week rolls.

doNotChase.name: Dalton Schultz
doNotChase.lead: The market is right about him, and it doesn't matter here.

case.label: The role
case.body: Collins is out again. Schultz has a 25.3% target share and drew 14 targets in the game Collins missed (DK Network).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Chem has one tight-end slot, and Likely holds it. The flex takes RB/WR only, so a second tight end scores you zero.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely on a Giants injury report. He isn't on this week's.

doNotChase.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
doNotChase.lead: A second tight end has no seat.

case.label: The fact
case.body: He scored 1.5 on Thursday in Atlanta's 35-14 win at Green Bay (carried from Friday's reporting, not re-searched).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: One tight-end slot, held by Likely. The flex is RB/WR only.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely getting hurt. Separately, the log grades the decline WRONG if Pitts outscores Likely in two of the next three weeks.

doNotChase.name: Jaxson Dart
doNotChase.lead: On injured reserve. The ownership is still leaving.

case.label: The fact
case.body: ESPN lists him on injured reserve and Winston is the starter (Giants.com, carried).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing. You start Josh Allen in a one-quarterback league.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage. Monangai (RB) and Boston (WR) are the weakest movable players and nobody clears either. Two weeks of data is thin, but the tool's answer stands and I didn't go looking for a reason to disagree.

settled.result: He missed Thursday, was limited Friday and is questionable. It hasn't cost anything yet; the first card covers it.

settled.title: Add the Lions D/ST (24 Sep)
settled.result: Dropped for the Vikings on 25 Sep before it played. Closed CHURN, not RIGHT or WRONG. Third D/ST since 23 Sep.

settled.title: Let Kyle Pitts go; Chem can't use a second tight end (23 Sep)
settled.result: Pitts scored 1.5 on Thursday. The structural reason stands.

settled.title: Hold Likely through the Giants' quarterback change (22 Sep)
settled.result: Winston starts and Likely led the Giants with 10 targets in Week 2 (week archive). The target clause is graded after Sunday.
